title: Towards Supporting QIR: Steps for Adopting the Quantum Intermediate Representation
problem: Quantum computing intermediate representations (IRs) are critical for optimization, but adoption pathways are unclear; converting existing simulators to support QIR requires significant effort.
motivation: QIR (built on LLVM) offers standardization benefits; understanding adoption steps reduces barriers to broader quantum simulator support of QIR and classical control flow.
method: The research team converted an existing quantum circuit simulator (a program that mimics quantum computer behavior) to use QIR—a standardized format for describing quantum operations. They tested several different adoption strategies and measured whether the new QIR-based version ran as fast as the original. They also demonstrated that using QIR enables classical control flow, meaning you can write regular programming logic (like if-statements or loops) mixed together with quantum instructions.
key_novelty: The paper demonstrates that quantum simulators can adopt QIR format without any performance loss while gaining the ability to mix regular programming logic with quantum operations (classical control flow).
contributions: Step-by-step guide for QIR runtime adoption
Quantum circuit simulator with QIR support
primary_theme: QIR adoption pathway for quantum circuit simulators
